messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED (P1) — runtime: repeated GPU OOMs during prefill on rtx-pool-7. Affected service: inference-api-prod. Pager: @alex.g oncall.

pagerduty: Incident created: PD-7862. Page sent to alex.g.

alex.g: on it. beginning triage — grabbing node/container logs and recent deploys.

alex.g: kubectl logs --tail=200 pod/inference-runtime-7g-2 -n prod | sed -n '1,200p'

alex.g: ```
[2026-03-15T16:02:11Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA out of memory when allocating 3.2G for prefill KV cache
[2026-03-15T16:02:11Z] runtime INFO: container restart triggered by OOMKill
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] allocator: free 0.5G, used 14.7G/15.2G
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] model: requested prefill tokens=12000, seq_len=12288, model=redwood-open-16k-qat
```

maria.h: seeing same in alerts. Grafana: sudden spike in restart_count for rtx-pool-7 and 8 starting ~16:00 UTC. 502 rate up for route /v1/generate?model=redwood-open-16k-qat from 0.3%->5%.

samir.p: quick guess — long prefill for huge prompts is exhausting GPU memory (KV cache growth). Might be pathological prompt or malicious. Any correlated client ids?

alex.g: query logs: 

alex.g: ```sql
select client_id, count(*) as calls from requests where model='redwood-open-16k-qat' and tokens_requested>8000 and timestamp>now()-1h group by client_id order by calls desc limit 20;
```

alex.g: top client_id: cust-839 (30 calls), cust-1012 (4 calls), the rest singletons. cust-839 appears to be sending long-context generative jobs.

nina.cs: @maria.h i have an open CS ticket from cust-839 about slow responses earlier — escalating now and telling them we're investigating restarts.

maria.h: temporarily setting alert to page SRE on 1% 502s for that route. want to reduce blast radius: suggestions for immediate mitigations?

samir.p: mitigation options (fast to do):
- route long-context requests to smaller model (8k variant) by setting routing override for cust-839
- clamp prefill tokens at runtime per-request (prefill_max_tokens=4096) via admin API
- disable prefill KV caching for the 16k model (will be slower but avoids large KV allocations)
- scale up gpus (slow) or cordon nodes (not ideal)

liz.t: can we flip a runtime flag without a full deploy? we have the admin endpoint to change model profiles: POST /admin/model_profiles/{model}/update with JSON. who can call it?

alex.g: I can hit admin. Doing first safe step: clamp prefill to 4k for the 16k model.

alex.g: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/model_profiles/redwood-open-16k-qat/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' -d '{"prefill_max_tokens":4096}'

deploy-bot: admin API: config change accepted for model redwood-open-16k-qat, new prefill_max_tokens=4096 (applied to running routers).

alex.g: patch applied. pushing routing override for cust-839 to map to redwood-open-8k-quant for now.

alex.g: ```yaml
# routing override
route: cust-839
override_model: redwood-open-8k-quant
reason: emergency mitigation - excessive prefill tokens
ttl: 2h
```

deploy-bot: routing override created for cust-839.

maria.h: CS notified cust-839 that we applied a temporary mitigation and asked for sample failing prompts. asked them to back off long-batched jobs.

samir.p: monitoring after change. watch for restart_count and 502s. also checking whether other custs will be affected by prefill clamp.

alex.g: immediate metrics: restart_count on rtx-pool-7 dropped from 8/hr to 0 in next 3 minutes. 502 rate for affected route reduced from 4.8% -> 0.6%. good sign.

liz.t: agree this buys time. next step: root cause patch — we need a safer prefill allocation path: if requested prefill * kv_size > gpu_free_memory * 0.6 then fall back to incremental prefill (CPU-backed) or reject with 4xx. who's on runtime to make a small hotfix?

samir.p: I can push a small runtime guard; will add a config ENV PREFILL_MB_LIMIT and a codepath to fail early with 429 if > limit OR stream prefill via CPU. estimate ~90m to code+unit tests and canary.

alex.g: do it. put canary to 10% traffic only for 16k model. I'll coordinate monitoring and rollback.

samir.p: creating branch: runtime/guard-prefill-429. patch includes: check_pre_fill() -> if required_kv_mb > PREFILL_MB_LIMIT then return ERROR(429, "prefill exceeds allowed memory, reduce tokens or use smaller model"). default PREFILL_MB_LIMIT=8000 (8GB).

samir.p: pushed commit abc1234 -> building image.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: runtime:guard-prefill-429 -> canary set to 10% on rtx-pool-9.

alex.g: monitoring canary: logs show prefill rejections for several large requests (429) from cust-XYZ — that's expected. node memory usage stable on canary nodes.

maria.h: CS: informing cust-839 that we've applied routing override and are working on runtime guard; provided ETA ~2h for full rollout.

nina.cs: cust-839 confirmed reduced failures on their side, they can throttle some jobs and will provide samples.

liz.t: good. any further customer-facing mitigation? rollback model to smaller default for some routes?

alex.g: did an emergency runbook step: disabled prefill KV caching for the 16k model as well (applied a toggle) to reduce memory pressure for any remaining traffic. command used: 

alex.g: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/model_profiles/redwood-open-16k-qat/update -d '{"kv_cache":false}'

deploy-bot: model profile updated: kv_cache false. Note: this increases token latency for long sessions.

samir.p: canary looks clean for 25 minutes now. starting gradual rollout to remaining nodes with rate limit and healthchecks. Will keep the prefill_max_tokens clamp in place.

deploy-bot: rollout to prod started: 3 nodes at a time, health window 3m.

alex.g: handoff in 30m. liz, samir — if anything degrades please wake me. maria/nina — continue customer updates. I'll assemble a short incident summary for postmortem.

maria.h: will update the incident ticket and CS thread. sending initial impact note to account team: affected 1 enterprise customer (cust-839) with elevated error and restarts between 16:00-16:40 UTC. temporary mitigations: routing override, prefill_max_tokens clamp (4k), disabled kv_cache for 16k model.

nina.cs: adding customer note: they want a follow-up call tomorrow to tune model choices.

samir.p: rollout finished at 16:42. production metrics: OOM restarts back to baseline, 99th p99 latency increased ~120ms for long sessions (expected), CPU prefill fallback not yet enabled (we're returning 429 for now).

deploy-bot: can confirm all runtime instances healthy.

alex.g: marking incident triage -> mitigation complete. will keep incident open for postmortem and follow-up tasks:
- create prompt-heuristics to detect and rate-limit dangerous prefill patterns
- add server-side prefill streaming fallback (CPU) to avoid OOMs
- add model-profile automated tests to simulate extreme prefill sizes
- update docs for customers on recommended model choices for large contexts

liz.t: added RFC ticket INF-RFC-214 to track prefill streaming and safe-fallback. assigned to samir.p and eng-runtime team.

maria.h: final customer note drafted and queued.

alex.g: handoff: I'm stepping off call at 17:05 UTC. oncall for next shift: liz.t. Liz, please pick up monitoring and CS coordination.

liz.t: acknowledged. thanks team. excellent coordinated response.

incident-bot: Incident PD-7862 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident channel will remain open until postmortem.

alex.g: closing thread for now; I'll post the short postmortem later today with timelines and root cause analysis.

maria.h: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
